scope_line: Scope: the openclaw monorepo (gateway, agents, channels, skills and Skill Workshop, plugins and extensions, MCP, Control UI, companion apps, QA and CI). ClawHub (separate repository) and team.openclaw.ai operations are out of scope.

MAL-01.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-02.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-03.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-04.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-05.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-06.evidence: Typed gateway methods with JSON output modes and MCP JSON output (docs/cli/mcp/json-output.md); no OpenAPI or dry-run for gateway mutations.
MAL-06.alt_note: The gateway protocol is typed end to end.

MAL-07.evidence: Canvas serves agent-authored documents and widgets (src/canvas); Control UI layout is code.
MAL-07.alt_note: Canvas is AI-authored, validated UI as data.

MAL-08.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD views (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-10.evidence: Cron jobs, hooks, routing bindings and auto-reply configuration are declared as data (docs/gateway/config-hooks.md, config-automation.md, src/routing, src/auto-reply); no general rules engine with a test mode.
MAL-10.alt_note: Routing and automation cover many entities through configuration.

MAL-11.evidence: Inbound webhook hooks trigger agent runs; audit events record runs, messages and tool actions; no outbound subscriptions with retry.

MAL-12.evidence: Hook scripts run in the gateway process; agent tools for non-main sessions run in sandboxes governed by tool policy and elevated mode (docs/gateway/sandboxing.md, sandbox-vs-tool-policy-vs-elevated.md).
MAL-12.alt_note: Sandboxing with tool policy isolates agent-written code.

GOV-01.evidence: No automated accessibility scanning found for the Control UI or companion apps.

GOV-02.evidence: Audit event store records agent runs, messages and tool actions with queries and configuration (src/audit/audit-event-types.ts, docs/gateway/audit.md); the Skill Workshop keeps an append-only proposal event ledger (docs/tools/skill-workshop/proposals.md). Configuration changes are not audit events.
GOV-02.alt_note: Skill definitions and their approvals are fully audited.

GOV-03.evidence: Local-first storage, trajectory export and cleanup (src/trajectory/export.ts, cleanup.ts), and redacted diagnostics export (docs/gateway/health.md:56); not driven by tags.

GOV-04.evidence: Exec approvals with allowlists, DM pairing, tool policies, sandboxing and a secrets subsystem (docs/tools/exec-approvals.md, src/pairing, src/secrets); CodeQL, dependency audit and security review workflows (.github/workflows/codeql.yml, dependency-audit.yml, security-review.yml).

GOV-05.evidence: Workshop skill collections are backed up and can be restored or rolled back with revision hashes (src/skills/workshop/collection-backup.ts, collection-restore.ts, collection-rollback.ts); configuration has rotating backups and recovery (src/config/backup-rotation.ts, recovery-policy.ts) but no operator rollback with diffs. Under the inventory rule a 3 needs every default surface at 3.

GOV-06.evidence: Skill changes are typed proposals (PROPOSAL.md with revision hashes) that the agent or a person creates; evaluations are stored on the exact revision and apply revalidates the evaluated tree (docs/tools/skill-workshop/proposals.md, src/skills/workshop/service-propose.ts, service-evaluation.ts); the system agent turns chat into proposals for configuration commands with approval classification (src/system-agent/approval-intent.ts).
GOV-06.alt_note: Evidence attaches automatically once an evaluator plugin is installed; none is bundled.

GOV-07.evidence: Defaults are autonomous.mode auto and approvalPolicy auto (src/skills/workshop/config.ts:15-20), so proposals apply without a person; evaluator block decisions only exist if an evaluator plugin is installed. Setting approvalPolicy to pending gives a per-class approval policy.

GOV-08.evidence: Doctor repairs and migrates configuration (docs/gateway/doctor.md), a compatibility layer (src/compat) and a plugin activation boundary test (src/plugin-activation-boundary.test.ts) around a versioned plugin SDK (src/plugin-sdk).

ARC-01.rationale: Agent runtime: generic-store query performance (fixed per-archetype rule).

ARC-05.rationale: Scope fact multi_tenant is false: A personal assistant per installation; shared gateways carry several people but are not isolated tenants (VISION.md).

ARC-06.rationale: Scope fact hosted_service is false: A personal gateway daemon, not a multi-user service.

DEL-02.evidence: Gateway, Control UI and macOS, iOS and Android companion apps are separate deployables with their own release workflows (apps/, .github/workflows/android-release.yml, ios-release-e2e.yml).

DEL-03.evidence: Separate TypeScript projects for core, extensions, UI and scripts (tsconfig.core.json, tsconfig.extensions.projects.json) and a plugin activation boundary test (src/plugin-activation-boundary.test.ts).

DEL-05.evidence: CI runs on pull requests with CodeQL, dependency audit, E2E and performance checks, but passive draft pull requests are isolated from the main slots (.github/workflows/ci.yml:82-93); no accessibility check.

MAL-13.evidence: Plugins and extensions for channels, providers, tools and memory through a plugin SDK, declarative skills, hooks and an MCP registry (docs/cli/mcp/registry.md); ClawHub is the skill and plugin registry.

MAL-14.evidence: Agent tools can run sandboxed under tool policy; plugins and hooks run in the gateway process with full trust.

MAL-15.evidence: Control UI, doctor, diagnostics export, logs and a QA lab (qa/) let developers validate against a live gateway.

MAL-19.evidence: MCP channel-bridge server exposing channel tools (src/mcp/channel-server.ts, channel-tools.ts), an MCP registry and a typed gateway protocol.

MAL-20.evidence: Users complete tasks conversationally across messaging channels with tool actions; operators configure OpenClaw in natural language through the system agent, which plans one safe command and waits for approval of the pending proposal (src/system-agent/assistant.ts, approval-intent.ts); skills are authored in chat.

GOV-09.evidence: Pairing identities for senders, exec approvals previewing commands, tool policies, sandboxing, idempotency keys on gateway methods (94 non-test files under src/gateway) and audit events for tool actions.

MAL-16.evidence: Channel plugins map WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Signal and others onto one canonical message model (src/channels); providers map onto one model interface.

MAL-17.evidence: The plugin SDK covers channel auth and pairing, inbound and outbound sync and install and configure lifecycle (src/plugin-sdk, custodian-skills/configure-channel).

MAL-18.evidence: A compatibility layer and doctor migrations keep older configuration working; no public deprecation windows.

EXP-01.evidence: Kernel of gateway sessions (conversation), channels (channel), pairing and auth (identity), tool policy (permission), cron, hooks and flows (workflow), and memory and files (content).

EXP-02.evidence: About 50 domain skills ship as bundles on an unchanged kernel (skills/: notion, obsidian, github, trello, spotify-player and more), and the agent authors new ones. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: If skills are judged too small to count as domains.
EXP-02.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 4 on the evidence above.

EXP-03.evidence: Skills are versioned, installable bundles installed through ClawHub and the CLI (skills/clawhub, src/cli/skills-cli.ts).

LRN-01.evidence: Audit events for runs, messages and tool actions are written as they happen and are queryable (src/audit/audit-event-queries.ts); a runtime trajectory store records sessions (src/trajectory/runtime-store.sqlite.test.ts).

LRN-02.evidence: Experience-review observations and evaluation findings are stored on the proposal revision they concern and recorded in the append-only proposal event ledger (src/skills/workshop/experience-review*.ts, docs/tools/skill-workshop/proposals.md). Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Observations come from sessions, not from users.
LRN-02.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

LRN-04.evidence: Trajectories export for offline analysis; no joined usage, support and delivery models.
LRN-04.alt_note: The experience review mines session history continuously.

LRN-06.evidence: The experience review scheduler turns observed runs into skill proposals when the system is idle (src/skills/workshop/experience-review-scheduler.ts, experience-review.ts, proposal-generation.ts); proposals are evidence-backed but not ranked by expected impact.
LRN-06.alt_note: Proposals carry their originating experience as evidence.

DEL-04.evidence: By default the autonomous experience review drafts and applies skill proposals (autonomous.mode auto, approvalPolicy auto, src/skills/workshop/config.ts:15-20), under the Workshop's policy, revisions and rollback. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Changes apply per installation, not across tenants.
DEL-04.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

LRN-09.evidence: Evaluator hooks compare each candidate with the complete baseline skill and store metrics and a pass, revise or block decision on the exact revision (docs/tools/skill-workshop/proposals.md); no evaluator is bundled (none in extensions/) and nothing observes impact after apply.
LRN-09.alt_note: Baseline, metric and decision are recorded per proposal once an evaluator is installed.

DEL-06.evidence: Health monitor, status commands with JSON output, and a diagnostics export with sanitised status and health snapshots and the configuration shape (docs/gateway/health.md:13-65).

DEL-07.evidence: Docker, Fly and Render deployment definitions (fly.toml, render.yaml, deploy/) and CI test boxes (.github/workflows/ci-check-testbox.yml); no per-change ephemeral environment with seeded data.
DEL-07.alt_note: CI test boxes are ephemeral per change.

DEL-08.evidence: Live and E2E checks across channels and apps (.github/workflows/openclaw-live-and-e2e-checks-reusable.yml), and a maturity scorecard generated from a taxonomy and QA evidence covering 280 capability areas (docs/maturity/scorecard.md, taxonomy.yaml, qa/).

LRN-07.evidence: With autonomous.mode auto by default, the experience review scheduler turns observed runs into skill proposals when the system is idle (src/skills/workshop/experience-review-scheduler.ts, proposal-generation.ts).
LRN-07.alt_note: The curator tracks which skills persist.

LRN-08.evidence: Proposals are scanned before apply (src/skills/workshop/proposal-scan.ts), and evaluator hooks can compare against the baseline and block, but no evaluator ships (none in extensions/).

ARC-02.evidence: The workshop store has a versioned SQLite schema (src/skills/workshop/store-sqlite-schema.ts) and doctor migrates configuration; no down steps.

ARC-08.evidence: Agents can declare model fallbacks (src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts); plugins run in-process, so a 3 is not defensible under the inventory rule.

ARC-09.evidence: Backup covers state, configuration, credentials, workspaces, agents and managed skills (src/commands/backup-shared.ts:76), with verification, scheduling and a restore test that round-trips into a fresh target with a matching inventory (src/commands/backup-restore.test.ts:176). Private captures are excluded by design. No recovery objectives are stated (level 4).

DEL-01.evidence: The /learn command turns a request into requirements and sources and stages a pending skill proposal for review, revising existing Workshop skills before creating new ones (src/skills/workshop/learn-prompt.ts). No acceptance criteria or risk class.
DEL-01.alt_note: A pending, reviewed draft that accounts for existing skills approaches level 3.

DEL-09.evidence: Skill proposals apply to the whole installation; there are no cohorts.

DEL-10.evidence: Autonomous mode and individual skills can be switched off in configuration at runtime (src/skills/workshop/config.ts).

LRN-03.evidence: The experience review observes failed runs and corrections (src/skills/workshop/experience-review.ts).

LRN-05.evidence: openclaw doctor diagnoses configuration and runtime problems; experience review attaches the observed runs to proposals.

GOV-10.evidence: Workshop policy limits proposal size and origins (src/skills/workshop/policy.ts, proposal-origin-validation.ts); there is no per-period or blast-radius limit.

GOV-11.evidence: Every proposal records its origin agent, session, run and message (src/skills/workshop/proposal-origin-validation.ts) and is scanned before apply (proposal-scan.ts); with approvalPolicy auto, session content alone can drive an applied change.
GOV-11.alt_note: Provenance and scanning meet level 3 apart from the default auto-apply.

EXP-04.evidence: Unserved requests stay in session history.

EXP-05.evidence: Experience review proposes skills for observed tasks, not capabilities nobody has used yet.

EXP-06.evidence: New skills apply to the whole installation at once.

ARC-03.rationale: Scope fact hosted_service is false: A personal gateway daemon, not a multi-user service.

ARC-04.rationale: Scope fact hosted_service is false: A personal gateway daemon, not a multi-user service.

ARC-07.rationale: Scope fact hosted_service is false: A personal gateway daemon, not a multi-user service.

DEL-11.rationale: Scope fact code_release_path is false: The self-improvement path changes skills, not OpenClaw code.

limits: Repository evidence only, main at the tip named above. ClawHub (registry and scanning) is a separate repository. No evaluator plugin is bundled, so measurement depends on third-party or user plugins. The experience review was read from code and tests, not run. Single rater.
reading: **SAL 2**, joint highest. /learn turns a request into a pending skill proposal (DEL-01 2), and the experience review drafts and applies skills from observed runs (LRN-07 3), so both core loops reach L2. Backup and restore are verified and tested across state, configuration, credentials and skills (ARC-09 3). **Blocks L3:** configuration has only rotating backups, not operator rollback (GOV-05 2, inventory); skill changes have no staged exposure (DEL-09 1); the default auto-apply has no declared blast-radius limit (GOV-10 2).

persistent_data.evidence: Skills, memory, workshop state (SQLite) and configuration on disk.

schema_changes.evidence: The workshop store has a versioned SQLite schema (src/skills/workshop/store-sqlite-schema.ts) and doctor migrates configuration.

multi_tenant.evidence: A personal assistant per installation; shared gateways carry several people but are not isolated tenants (VISION.md).

hosted_service.evidence: A personal gateway daemon, not a multi-user service.

machine_actions.evidence: Agent tools and the gateway API change skills, configuration and channels.

agent_mutations.evidence: The experience review drafts and applies skill proposals (src/skills/workshop/experience-review.ts).

evolution_auto_apply.evidence: autonomous.mode auto and approvalPolicy auto are the defaults (src/skills/workshop/config.ts:15-20).

definition_change_path.evidence: Skills, memory and configuration are its definitions.

code_release_path.evidence: The self-improvement path changes skills, not OpenClaw code.
